plugins.description: Bandeja de soporte de WhatsApp: mapea cada conversacion a un proyecto, define hasta donde puede actuar el agente en cada una, y abre las tarjetas por contenido del mensaje. Se vincula escaneando un codigo QR y mantiene su propia conexion con WhatsApp: guarda lo que llega en un almacen local que el agente consulta, y contesta por esa misma conexion sin abrir ni enfocar ninguna ventana. Ya no depende de la app de escritorio de macOS ni de una pestana de WhatsApp Web.

Since 0.6.0 it also shows where your Claude usage goes, per model and per account, and can pick the model and effort each piece of work needs: a cheap model for simple work, a strong one for hard work, and never below your session's own model in a client's repository, on sensitive or failing work, or when Jev is unsure. It starts by only measuring; switching models is opt-in per account. Judges what your agents are about to run, before they run it, and stays out of the way otherwise: npm test, rm -rf node_modules and a push of your own branch pass without a word. When Jev (TypeSafe) sees risk, it advises the agent directly, naming what would be affected and a safe alternative, so you are not interrupted; only a team policy you set to require a person ever asks you. The judgement takes a few hundred milliseconds rather than a large model reasoning about your shell, and a set of local rules stops force pushes, recursive deletes from / or $HOME, dropped tables and curl | bash in about a millisecond with no network and no API key at all. How strict it is depends on where you are: the destination catalog is built from the worktrees Orca already knows about, so a client's repository is judged more carefully than your own tooling. Verified on macOS; Windows and Linux are implemented but untested.
